=== DOCS-TRUTH SUMMARY (verified 2026-06-08 against trino.io/docs/467) ===
• date_diff-MIN-MAX-in-HAVING: legal Trino — HAVING accepts any boolean expression that evaluates per-group (i.e. composed of aggregates and grouping columns). `HAVING date_diff('day', MIN(x), MAX(x)) > 365` is the same structural shape as the docs example `HAVING sum(acctbal) > 5700000` — both apply a scalar-comparison to an aggregate expression. Verified via WebFetch trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html: 'The HAVING clause is used in conjunction with aggregate functions and the GROUP BY clause to control which groups are selected.' `date_diff(unit, MIN(d), MAX(d))` is `bigint`-typed via aggregates; the `> 365` comparison is the per-group filter.
• two-level AVG-COUNT-DISTINCT: nested aggregates are NOT allowed directly in Trino (`AVG(COUNT(DISTINCT product_id))` is a parse-time error — same restriction as Postgres/Snowflake/Firebird, verified via WebSearch). REQUIRED rewrite is the **inner-CTE-then-outer-aggregate** pattern: inner CTE computes per-group `COUNT(DISTINCT x)`, outer query applies `AVG()` to the projected alias. Same class as the documented macro-average two-level shape (iter656 lock + r07:999 'aggregate inside its own scalar subquery' pattern).
• dim-join-SUM (currency-rates style): standard star-schema fact-times-dim JOIN + SUM(fact_col * dim_col) is mechanical from r08:12/52-67/111 worked star-schema primitive — `SELECT SUM(o.amount * r.usd_rate) FROM orders o JOIN currency_rates r ON o.currency_code = r.currency_code` is the canonical 'apply per-row conversion via JOIN to a small dim'. r08:111 explicitly covers the 'JOIN at query time to the dimension' framing for current-value lookups (rates change too often to denormalize).
